case_name: Chandramouleshwar Prasad v Patna High Court and Others
facts: The petitioner, an Additional District and Sessions Judge in Bihar, challenges the validity of two orders: one transferring him from Arrah to Singhbhum, and another declaring respondents 3-5 as senior to him in the gradation list.
In September 1968, S.C. Chakravarty, the retiring District Judge of Arrah, was due to retire on September 30.
The High Court wanted Misra, respondent No. 3, to officiate in the vacancy, but the Government of Bihar appointed the petitioner as officiating District and Sessions Judge at Arrah temporarily.
The High Court transferred the petitioner to Singhbhum as Additional District and Sessions Judge on October 25, 1968.
The petitioner filed this Writ Petition on October 29, 1968, claiming reliefs.

The Bihar Civil List published in March 1968 shows the petitioner at serial No. 10, one Dharm Deva Narain Sinha at No. 11, Govind Mohan Misra, respondent No. 3 at No. 11, Choudhary Sia Saran Sinha, respondent No. 4 at No. 13 and Jagannath Prasad Singh, respondent No. 5 at No. 14.
The question of these persons being selected and as Additional District and Sessions Judges engaged the High Court as early as March 1962 when two vacancies occurred in that rank.
Among the four officers immediately below the said three persons, the High Court considered respondents 3 and 4 to be fit for promotion in preference to the other two for reasons given.

The High Court recommended G. M. Misra, respondent No. 3 and C. S. Sinha, respondent No. 4 as fit for promotion and suggested their posting as Additional District and Sessions Judges at Hazaribagh and at Arrah.

As Misra was then acting as Deputy Secretary, Legislative Assembly and C. S. Sinha was functioning as Under Secretary, Law Department, the High Court requested that they might be released to enable them to join their new posts.

The matter came up before the High Court once more in September 1962 and the Registrar wrote to the Secretary intimating that the forthcoming vacancy in the rank of Additional District and Sessions Judge on October 12, 1962 by retirement of an officer should be filled up by promoting Misra then Deputy Secretary, Legislative Assembly to act as Additional District and Sessions Judge of Hazaribagh with effect from the said date.
The Chief Minister agreed to this proposal on September 14, 1962.
Government accepted this recommendation and made the necessary notification of posting the petitioner and D. N. Sinha as Additional District and Sessions Judges on January 7, 1963.

As respondents 3 and 4 could not then take up their appointments as Additional District and Sessions Judges because they were not released from the Assembly and State Electricity Board the Government by letter dated November 7, 1963 addressed to the Accountant General, Bihar allowed respondents 3 and 4 to draw pay in the scale admissible to Additional District and Sessions Judges with effect from January 15, 1963.
The petitioner started functioning as Additional District and Sessions Judge at Darbhanga on January 23, 1963.
issues: Validity of the order transferring the petitioner from Arrah to Singhbhum
Validity of the direction declaring respondents 3-5 as senior to the petitioner in the gradation list
Whether the High Court's recommendation for promotion was valid and binding on the Government
petitioner_arguments: The direction or order of September 23, 1968 was in contravention of R. 16(b) and R. 16(d) of the Bihar-Superior Judicial Service Rules
The order of the High Court dated October 25, 1968 following close to the heels of the said Government notification amounted to his reduction in rank and was otherwise penal in nature

The direction of the High Court requiring S.C. Chakravarty the retiring District Judge of Arrah in September 1968 to hand over charge of his office to Govind Mohan Misra, respondent No. 3 by purporting to appoint him as officiating District and Sessions Judge was a discriminatory order contravening Arts. 14, 16 and 311 of the Constitution
respondent_arguments: The High Court's recommendation for promotion was valid and binding on the Government
The petitioner had been passed over only about a month back and the question of re-considering his case did not at the moment arise
The respondents 3 and 4 were fit for promotion in preference to the other two for reasons given
court_reasoning: The Court found that the High Court's recommendation for promotion was valid and binding on the Government
The Court held that the direction or order of September 23, 1968 was not in contravention of R. 16(b) and R. 16(d) of the Bihar-Superior Judicial Service Rules

The Court rejected the petitioner's contention that the order of the High Court dated October 25, 1968 following close to the heels of the said Government notification amounted to his reduction in rank and was otherwise penal in nature
holding: The petition is allowed. The order transferring the petitioner from Arrah to Singhbhum is set aside. The direction declaring respondents 3-5 as senior to the petitioner in the gradation list is also set aside.
cases_cited: Chandramouleshwar Prasad v Patna High Court
Judge. It was pointed out by this Court in State of Assam v. Ranga
